name: How do I know if my deck substructure is still sound enough for new boards?

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my deck substructure is still sound enough for new boards?

acceptedAnswer.text: Determining the soundness of your deck's substructure (joists, beams, posts) is critical before installing new boards. Signs of a compromised substructure include visible rot, widespread cracking, excessive sagging, or movement when walked upon. A professional inspection is the most reliable way to assess its condition, as hidden damage can exist. Maine Results, Inc. always conducts a thorough inspection of your deck's existing framework once the old boards are removed, identifying any issues that need addressing to ensure the safety and longevity of your new deck surface.
acceptedAnswer.description: Assess your deck's substructure for rot, cracks, or sagging; a professional inspection is crucial to ensure it's sound enough for new boards.
